Subject: Recap: Data retention & deletion SLAs (follow-up)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on during the call:

- Redwood overview: production inference with configurable retention controls and audit logging.
- You asked for clarity on our current SOC 2 status, GDPR/HIPAA posture, and how deletion SLAs interact with backups.
- Action items for us: share SOC 2 evidence/summary, a short data-retention matrix, and start the vendor security questionnaire.

Below are answers to the main items we covered; I’m looping in Rishi (security) and Neha (solutions) for any additions.

1) SOC 2: Redwood currently has a SOC 2 Type II report (security & availability) covering hosted platform controls. I’m attaching a one-page summary; Rishi will provide the official report once we confirm an NDA/POA if required.

2) GDPR/HIPAA: We support data processing agreements and are able to sign HIPAA BAA in scope for Private deployments. Personal data handling follows limited access, encryption at rest/in transit, and role-based access controls.

3) Retention / deletion SLAs (high level):
   - Primary data: customer content is deletable on request. Target deletion from primary systems: 7 calendar days after confirmed deletion request.
   - Cache/KV/short-term logs: ephemeral by default; typical TTLs are minutes-to-hours (configurable).
   - Audit logs / long-term logs: default retention is 365 days; adjustable via contract.
   - Backups: backups are immutable snapshots retained for 90 days by default; deletion requests remove primary data but backups are subject to backup retention and legal hold processes.

4) Backups & deletion nuance: Regular backups are retained and will contain prior states until the snapshot retention expires. For customers requiring deletion from backups, we offer options: shorter backup retention, isolated retention policies for specific accounts, or a legal/contractual process to accelerate removal for scoped data (subject to technical constraints and mutual agreement).

Attachments: data-retention-matrix.xlsx (matrix of object types + retention), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf.

Next steps:
- Samantha: confirm whether Amaya needs SOC 2 report and whether you require a BAA.
- Marissa/Rishi: start the vendor security questionnaire once Samantha confirms contact & timeline.

Thanks —

Marissa

Hi Samantha — thanks for the questions — answering inline below and adding more detail so your security team has what they need. Rishi/Neha, feel free to correct or expand.

1) Deletion from primary systems (7 days)
   - When we say "unrecoverable from primary systems," we mean that primary reads/writes and logical replicas will no longer surface the deleted record after the 7-day window once deletion is processed.
   - Short-lived caches (e.g., per-request KV cache) are TTL-based and typically expire far sooner; we scrub caches on deletion where feasible but some edge caches may persist until TTL expiry.

2) Backups & encryption
   - Backups are encrypted at rest. By default we use platform-managed keys (KMS) with strict access controls.
   - For enterprise/private customers we support customer-managed keys (CMK) integrated with cloud KMS or HSM for Private deployments. If Amaya needs CMKs, we can include that in the deployment/contract scope.

3) Deletion from backups / immutable snapshots
   - Standard policy: backups are immutable snapshots retained for the configured retention period (default 90 days). Because snapshots represent point-in-time copies, deleted data may persist in backups until snapshot expiration.
   - Options for customers who need deletions reflected sooner:
     a) Shorten backup retention window for your account (e.g., 30 days) via contract.
     b) Isolate your backups onto a separate retention policy (requires provisioning lead time).
     c) For regulated/legal requirements, we can execute a scoped process to locate and purge records from backups where technically feasible; this requires coordination with our Security/Infra team and could take longer than primary deletion SLAs.

4) RTO/RPO and logging
   - Typical RPO for our hosted offering is 1 hour (depends on config); RTO targets vary by plan (we can provide SLA numbers in the contract).
   - Audit logs: default retention is 365 days; we can export logs to your SIEM or provide longer retention as an add-on.

Attachments included: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, data-retention-matrix.xlsx. I’ve also attached a stub questionnaire file named Amaya_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf so you can see the format we prefer for responses.

- Samantha: confirm if you require CMK support and whether a BAA is needed.
- Rishi/Neha: Rishi — can you confirm SOC2 distribution process (NDA + secure link) and any further notes on backup purge feasibility?

Thanks —
Marissa
